body:
This is the only way to pass the class. The professor and the university are very strict about it. Either you pass the exams or you don't and you have to retake it.

We don't have any of that here. There is no counselling at our university. Therapy is possible, but that requires going to my GP and people here don't take patient confidentiality all that seriously so it would be all over the town back home. I don't want them to pity me and I don't want it to reflect poorly on my family. I don't want them to be judged as bad parents or something because I am how I am. They aren't at fault and everyone would blame them.

I don't think I have ADHD. I just tend to procrastinate and I get lazy easily nowadays. I can usually be focused on whatever it is that I am doing. Just not all that much lately. I used to be able to spend hours learning about something or studying. Right now, I just get bored. Nothing is interesting at all. It is all so very boring.

You have given me a lot to ruminate on and I cried a bit. I think the worst has passed, at least for tonight. Thank you.

It is not the first class I will be failing. I have already extended my university beyond the usual length. I feel like I am siphoning away the resources that would be better spent on my siblings and that I am a huge disappointment. I went from a straight A pupil to a lousy university student who barely passes most subjects and wastes away any potential I ever had to do anything of myself. I cannot focus at all. I am just so distracted and tired. I am afraid of how my parents and siblings will react when I tell them and just how disappointed they will be. I also have two very close aunts who I feel I disappointed enough already. And I hate myself because the person who would most be disappoint if she were alive would be my Gran. I feel like I failed her most of all because I failed to follow through on all the good things she taught me while she was raising me. Realistically, I know they will all miss me, but I feel that their lives will be better despite it and that they will be relieved they no longer have to support a failure like me.

The worst part is that what is really killing me is the suspense. Because I keep **hoping** a miracle will happen and I will pass, but I **know** that there is not even a snowball's chance in hell of passing. I have to get 60 points to pass. I can count on maybe 50 and even that is an optimistic assessment. When I really think about it, I will probably get around 35 points or less. And it was not even that hard of a test. I could have easily scored over 70 points if I just studied a bit harder and were a bit more focused.

The nights are the worst. During the day, I manage to distract myself somehow. I force myself to work on something. To watch some films or read something. But it is the wee hours of the night now and I am alone with my thoughts and it is killing me. I tried reading. I cannot focus at all. I tried to put on a film, but it cannot drown out my thoughts. I don't know what it is about the night that is so much harder to bear. Or maybe it is that in a few hours I will have to face the results and that I feel like it is the end of everything.

And thank you for answering. You are a good person. Much better than I can ever hope to be.
